title: Chen-Chvátal Conjecture (Conjecture 1.1)
statement_text: Every metric space on $n$ points, where $n \geq 2$, either has at least $n$ distinct lines or has a universal line.
context_text: Chen and Chvátal proposed this conjecture as a generalisation of the classical result that $n$ non-collinear points in the Euclidean plane determine at least $n$ distinct lines, using betweenness-based lines in arbitrary metric spaces. The paper establishes a slightly stronger version — $\ell(G) + \mathrm{br}(G) \geq |G|$ — for the hereditary graph class $\mathcal{C}$, which contains all chordal graphs and all distance-hereditary graphs.
paper_contribution: Proves a strengthened form of the conjecture ($\ell(G)+\mathrm{br}(G)\geq|G|$) for all connected graphs $G\in\mathcal{C}\setminus\mathcal{F}$, where $\mathcal{C}$ is a hereditary class strictly containing chordal and distance-hereditary graphs.

title: Conjecture 2.2
statement_text: There is a finite set of graphs $F_0$ such that every connected graph $G \notin F_0$ either has a pendant edge or satisfies $\ell(G) + \mathrm{br}(G) \geq |G|$.
context_text: Let $G$ be a connected graph. For vertices $a,b,c$ of $G$, write $[abc]$ when $d(a,b)+d(b,c)=d(a,c)$ (shortest-path distance), i.e. $b$ lies between $a$ and $c$. The line induced by two distinct vertices $a,b$ is $\overline{ab}=\{a,b\}\cup\{x: [abx]\text{ or }[axb]\text{ or }[xab]\}$; $\ell(G)$ is the number of distinct lines of $G$, a line is universal if it contains all vertices, $\mathrm{br}(G)$ is the number of bridges (edges whose deletion disconnects $G$), $|G|$ the number of vertices, and a pendant edge is an edge incident to a vertex of degree one. The Chen–Chvátal conjecture (a metric version of the De Bruijn–Erdős theorem) asserts that every metric space on $n\ge2$ points has at least $n$ distinct lines or a universal line; for graph metrics, every bridge $ab$ satisfies $\overline{ab}=V(G)$, so counting each bridge as a separate line, $\ell(G)+\mathrm{br}(G)\ge|G|$ is a strengthening of the conjecture. The authors prove $\ell(G)+\mathrm{br}(G)\ge|G|$ for every connected graph $G$ outside the six graphs $C_4$, $K_{2,3}$, $W_4$ and three other small graphs, in the class of graphs all of whose induced subgraphs are chordal, have a cut-vertex, or have a non-trivial module (this class contains chordal and distance-hereditary graphs). As observed by Yori Zwols, the inequality is false for infinitely many graphs: replacing a bridge of a counter-example by a path of arbitrary length gives another counter-example. In the three known minimal counter-examples containing a bridge, the bridge is a pendant edge, which motivates excluding graphs with a pendant edge; any such family $F_0$ must contain the known exceptions. The authors also propose the variant that $\ell(G)+\mathrm{ul}(G)\ge|G|$ for every connected graph $G$, where $\mathrm{ul}(G)$ is the number of pairs of vertices inducing a universal line.

title: Conjecture 2.3
context_text: Here $\mathrm{ul}(G)$ denotes the number of pairs of vertices in $G$ that induce a universal line. This variant replaces the bridge count by the universal-line-pair count; it is stronger than the original Chen-Chvátal conjecture in that it does not dismiss graphs with universal lines as trivial, and no counter-example is known to this conjecture.

title: Open question on counter-examples to ℓ(G)+br(G)≥|G|
statement_text: It remains unknown whether all counter-examples to $\ell(G) + \mathrm{br}(G) \geq |G|$ can be obtained from a finite set of graphs by replacing a bridge by a path of arbitrary length.
context_text: Let $G$ be a connected graph. For vertices $a,b,c$ of $G$, write $[abc]$ when $d(a,b)+d(b,c)=d(a,c)$ (shortest-path distance), i.e. $b$ lies between $a$ and $c$.
